cards.info: What is a right-skewed distribution?
cards.backInfo: A distribution where the tail extends toward the larger values on the right.

cards.info: In a right-skewed distribution, what is the typical relationship between mean and median?
cards.backInfo: The mean is typically greater than the median.

cards.info: In a left-skewed distribution, what is the typical relationship between mean and median?
cards.backInfo: The mean is typically less than the median.

cards.info: In a perfectly symmetric distribution, what is the relationship between mean and median?
cards.backInfo: The mean and median are typically equal.

cards.info: How do outliers affect the mean?
cards.backInfo: The mean is very sensitive and is pulled toward the extreme values.

cards.info: Why is the median a better measure when outliers are present?
cards.backInfo: It is robust and much less affected by extreme values than the mean.

cards.info: What is the definition of standard deviation?
cards.backInfo: A measure of the average spread of data points relative to the mean.

cards.info: How does adding an outlier far from the mean affect standard deviation?
cards.backInfo: It typically increases the standard deviation of the data set.

cards.info: What is the range, and is it heavily affected by outliers?
cards.backInfo: The difference between max and min values; it is highly affected by outliers.

cards.info: What feature should you observe to judge standard deviation in a graph?
cards.backInfo: The horizontal width of the distribution, not the height of the graph.

cards.info: If a distribution has a 'tail' on the right, what type is it?
cards.backInfo: A right-skewed distribution.

cards.info: Why is the mean usually greater than the median in right-skewed data?
cards.backInfo: Large values in the right tail pull the mean toward the right.

cards.info: If the mean is less than the median, what is the likely distribution shape?
cards.backInfo: A left-skewed distribution.

cards.info: Where are the mean and median located in a symmetric distribution?
cards.backInfo: They are usually at the same central position and equal in value.

cards.info: What happens to the mean if a very large outlier is removed?
cards.backInfo: The mean will decrease significantly as it is no longer pulled upward.

cards.info: Which statistic is least affected by outliers on the SAT?
cards.backInfo: The median.

cards.info: What happens to standard deviation as data points cluster closer to the center?
cards.backInfo: It decreases because the average distance to the mean is smaller.

cards.info: What is the common effect of adding an outlier on standard deviation and range?
cards.backInfo: Both measures typically increase.

cards.info: How do you calculate the range of a data set?
cards.backInfo: Subtract the minimum value from the maximum value.

cards.info: What visual trap should be avoided when comparing standard deviations?
cards.backInfo: Do not assume a taller graph means a larger standard deviation; check horizontal spread.
